messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — after bringing up q4 quant for candidate-2026c (small-ish LLaMA-deriv), we see a regression on multilingual BLEU for ja->en and zh->en in the nightly eval: ja->en -4.2 BLEU, zh->en -3.8. Seems correlated with mixed-width lines (CJK + halfwidth katakana/emoji).

sahil: can you paste a short failing example and tokenizer outputs?

maya: sure, sample input we used:

"今日は学校🏫 at 10:00 — 来てね" (ja mixed kanji + ascii + emoji)

Model (q4) output: "Today school at 10:00 — come." (missing nuance)
Model (fp16 baseline) output: "Today, please come to school at 10:00." (better)

Tokenization diff (our `redwood-tokenize`):
```
# fp16 tokens: [今日は, 学校, 🏫, at, 10, :, 00, —, 来, て, ね]
# q4 tokens:  [今日, は学校, 🏫, at, 10, :, 00, —, 来て, ね]
```
Notice different merges: `は学校` vs `学校` boundary and `来て` vs `来, て` — these shifts can change prefix stats and generation.

lei: that's odd — quantization shouldn't change tokenizer outputs. Did we change tokenization pipeline or normalization (NFKC/NFC) in the build step? Which tokenizer artifact did the q4 job pull?

maya: q4 runtime used `tokenizer_v2.tar.gz` built from commit `d4b7c9f` earlier today. Baseline uses `tokenizer_v1` (older). I ran a direct tokenization-only check on the artifact and got the q4-style merges. I'll paste the exact commands:

```
# reproduce
python -m redwood.tokenize --artifact s3://redwood-artifacts/tokenizer_v2.tar.gz --text "今日は学校🏫 at 10:00 — 来てね" --show-merges
```

ana: eval-bot ran the full WMT-ish harness, attached run id `eval-2026-03-15-42`. Link: https://ci.redwood/eval/2026/42

ops-bot: perf snapshot for that run: p50 42ms, p95 220ms, memory 3.1GB — nothing abnormal.

sahil: two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer artifact build inadvertently used a different unicode normalization (we switched to NFKC for emoji handling last week); 2) our tokenizer pipeline changed BPE merge order when building vocab because of different byte-level pretokenization for multibyte UTF-8 runs — maybe a bug in the packaging script that used `latin1` fallback for some byte ranges.

jen: owners? we should triage today — impacting nightly regression. @lei can you own root-cause? If it's tokenizer packaging we can roll back to v1 for nightly.

lei: I'll take it. Plan: run tokenizer-only diff across ~1k multilingual lines, compare merges, then binary-search commits between v1 and v2 to find offending change.

maya: adding a quick check: I ran `python -c 'import unicodedata; print(unicodedata.normalize("NFKC","🏳️‍🌈"))'` and results differ between the two build envs — environment Python/icu differences could explain.

sahil: good catch. also add a test in CI: tokenization-stability for mixed-width grapheme clusters (include emoji ZWJ sequences, halfwidth katakana, fullwidth ascii) with exact merge hash.

lei: will add test, and if we confirm packaging bug we'll cut v2.1 with same vocab but proper normalization.

maya: running the 1k-line diff now, will post logs + failing commit hash in thread.

ana: once we have repro, I'll re-run eval to confirm fix. eval-bot queued.

ops-bot: created incident INC-2026-138 for tracking (low-sev).

sahil: note for postmortem — quant bring-up should be strictly model-weight-only. Ensure tokenizer artifact pinned by commit hash in recipes.

maya: thanks everyone — updating in 30m :eyes:

(eval-bot): queued job eval-2026-03-15-42 started

jen: :thumbsup:

lei: taking ownership, assigning follow-ups to tokenization epic.
